_meta.title: Estate Subsystem — Sir Abisec of Stapleford (Knight Banneret of Hindon)
_meta.authoritative: This JSON is the AUTHORITATIVE source for ALL estate numbers — cash, income, expenses, improvements, fortification DV, settlement & military demographics. estate.md is prose companion only; on any numeric conflict, THIS file wins.
_meta.currency: Tracked to GBP 0.1 (decimals of a pound). 1 GBP = 20 shillings (s) = 240 denarii (d). Convert windfalls/wages/ransoms to GBP at the moment of entry.
_meta.reconcile_cadence: Reconciled each WINTER PHASE (Step 4 economic + Step 8 Glory). Mid-year: append an ad-hoc cash.ledger entry for every windfall, grant, wage, plunder, or capital project, keeping the running balance current. The world-tick 'estate & entourage' hook fires this.

rules.customary_revenue: CR per holding = sum of income lines (assized rents + production + court/market + improvement yields). CR = the Honour value (Ruling #26b). Annual Land Glory = CR, capped 100/yr (Ruling #26e). Baron tier = Honour 200-300.
rules.expenses: Itemized CONCRETELY, never a flat 55/25/10/10 (that default over-stated a frugal lord). Categories: Army (the dominant real cost — eschille, garrison, warhorses, arms, castle ward), Court (admin + hospitality), Family (ACTUAL dependents only). Abisec is Temperate 13 / Modest 13 — he lives lean, so expenses run well under the old default and the estate BANKS a surplus.
rules.operating_surplus: operating_surplus = CR - expenses_total. Banked to liquid each Winter Phase reconciliation.
rules.liquid_cash: cash.liquid_gbp is the running balance, to 0.1. EVERY windfall, grant, wage, and capital project is logged in cash.ledger with its delta and the resulting running balance.
rules.improvements: Each improvement: build_cost (one-time, paid from liquid), annual_yield (added to the holding's CR), space (land/sites it occupies), risk (e.g., cattle murrain = an annual roll), status (built/planned).
rules.fortification_DV: Per element, KAP Defence Value. Wet moat adds to the ditch's DV. Updated as works complete; tower cadence = one wooden tower (GBP 15) per season, no debt.
rules.maintenance_glory: Winter Phase Step 8: maintenance Glory = libra ACTUALLY spent on conspicuous display/largesse. Frugal Abisec spends little, so this is LOW (the deliberate trade-off for banking cash). NOT the same as total upkeep.
rules.economic_grade: Set by ESTABLISHMENT (castle + CR + household), NOT by personal splurge. Abisec is Superlative (castle + GBP 67 CR + a banneret's household) and stays so while living frugally — keeping the +2 horse / +3 family Winter-Phase modifiers.

military._rules: Book of the Estate (player-authoritative): servitium = 1 knight + 3 foot per £10 CR + 1 foot per remaining £1; a £50+ estate fields an ESCHILLE (5-15 mounted + 10-30 foot). GARRISON MANNING is by Table 5.5 (min professionals / max defenders per fortification), NOT by income.

servitium_debitum.computation: £55 CR -> 5 knights + 15 foot (1kn+3foot/£10 at £50) + 5 foot (1 foot per £1 over £50) = 5 knights + 20 foot. Split per the £50-rule (10 field + 5 king's-garrison at £50; the +5 remainder foot are field) -> 15 field + 5 king's-garrison.
servitium_debitum.shortfall_fine: Not bringing the 5 owed knights to a muster = a fine, £1 up to the holding's annual value, by the King's anger.
servitium_debitum.maintenance_rates: knights £4 ea, foot £0.5 ea; a lowered servitium frees that saved maintenance to spend at will.
servitium_debitum.maintenance_cost_gbp: 5 knights @ £4 (all-in: fee+horse+arms) = £20 + 20 foot @ £0.5 = £10 -> £30/yr. (Lord pays no fee to himself; in practice = 5 household knights £20 + 20 foot £10 = £30. He provisions all 20 foot even though 5 serve a royal castle.)

kings_garrison.ruling: [Fate No 82, autumn 483] Uther does NOT defer — the 5 king's-garrison foot serve at the nearest ROYAL castle, not Hindon. The rule allows deferral; the King declines it (spends Abisec, gifts nothing). Re-petition possible later.
kings_garrison.effect: Hindon's own foot = 15 (the field foot); the 5 king's-garrison serve the Crown elsewhere.

eschille.definition: Abisec's single field tactical unit (£50+ estate): the lord + knight-officers + other household knights + ~10 professional foot (payrolled, trained, best armour after a victory).
eschille.note: Servitium owes 5 mounted (lord + 4); Abisec keeps 6 (himself + 5 household knights) — the 6th is his OWN extra knight, his to field or not.
eschille.dispersal_note: The 6 lances are chronically SCATTERED (envoys, escorts, Salisbury). The standing problem is CONCENTRATION, not headcount — keep the eschille together as a riding force.

peripheral_swords.note: household knight, but currently STAYED at Salisbury (Roderick's court)

peripheral_swords.name: Sir Jasson
peripheral_swords.note: friendly NEIGHBOUR knight — rides with Abisec by goodwill, not homage (brought lances to the Ebble)

military.squire: Achil of Stapleford (brother & heir) — knighting ~484 on the Saxon campaign (Uther's counsel: blood him in real war; keep him a LORD as well as a knight; let him keep the healer-craft).

foot_and_garrison.captain_castellan: Drustan — grizzled veteran sergeant-at-arms / garrison-captain UNDER the lord; minds the foot & holds Hindon when Abisec rides. Abisec sits Hindon himself (no castellan title).

garrison_table_5_5._rules: Table 5.5 — min PROFESSIONALS to man the wall / MAX defenders the wall can hold. SIEGE minimums, not peacetime standing.

castle_keep_bailey.fortification: Motte-and-bailey Castle (shell keep on motte; ~1000 ft, 2 acres)

garrison_table_5_5.gap_note: Siege ideal ~25 professionals (10 castle + 15 town); Abisec has 15 foot (the King kept the garrison-5). The shortfall is filled by the TOWN'S OWN MILITIA on the town walls — but Hindon is UNDER the professional ideal: a real siege leans hard on the town turning out and on the drawbridge sealing keep from town.

town_furnishes.obligation: watch-and-ward — the wool-town garrisons its OWN walls at no cost to the lord.
town_furnishes.militia_realistic: ~45 households (~200 souls) -> ~50-90 able-bodied townsmen (burgher militia). NOT the table's 300 'max defenders' — that is the WALL'S capacity, not the town's population.
town_furnishes.professional_core: Table 5.5 wants 15 professionals to stiffen 1500 ft of town wall; a town this size cannot keep 15 professionals, so Abisec's foot must supply the trained core. NET: the town furnishes BODIES (its militia, free); the lord furnishes the PROFESSIONAL stiffening.
town_furnishes.key_burghers: Gwgan the Wool-master (guild voice) + the chartered watch.

garrison_distribution.peacetime: a light ward: the town's rotating watch on the town walls; ~3-5 foot + Drustan on the castle; the balance of the 15 foot drilling/patrolling/escorting (and available as field foot).
garrison_distribution.siege: concentrate all 15 foot (~10 castle + ~5 stiffening the town gate/towers) + the town militia (~50-90) on the town walls + raise the drawbridge to seal keep from town. The 2 wooden towers enfilade the town wall & gate.
garrison_distribution.ruling_note: Per-wall manning is a GM ruling — KAP sizes garrison by Table 5.5 (whole-fortification), not per wall-yard.

subinfeudation.policy: RARE & costly for a one-caput banneret; landholding knights rarely exceed 20% (reputation). Abisec CANNOT afford to enfeoff a war-band (player's correct economics vs Uther's count-scale advice).
subinfeudation.current: Stapleford (£12) settled on Achil/heir — owes Abisec 1 knight + 3 foot once Achil is belted (grows the field force at no cash cost).
subinfeudation.note: The garrison fix is DOCTRINE (right-size with foot + the town watch + a castellan), NOT more sub-enfeoffment.

military.warhorses: Karu (Charger 6d6), a Courser (6d6), 2 Rouncey (4d6), a Sumpter

officers.constable: a household knight holds the Constable office (horses ready — eschille doctrine)
officers.castellan: NONE — Abisec SITS Hindon himself as resident lord-commander. Drustan (garrison-captain/sergeant-at-arms) holds it in the lord's absence (musters/war); no separate castellan office for a one-caput banneret.

former_men.name: Sir Gwion
former_men.note: garrisoned Vagon; when Vagon reverted to Roderick (spring 482) Gwion STAYED with it — now Roderick's man, NO LONGER Abisec's.

provisioning.summary: Abisec's establishment is part-provisioned through STAPLEFORD (the family seat), keeping Hindon's frugal Army line (£32) tight against the £30 rules-cost of 5 knights + 20 foot.
provisioning.armory: Stapleford's armory (Selyf; net +£1, PRODUCES arms) outfits the household — so Hindon's effective arms/armour outlay is below the £3 line; much is made at home.
provisioning.surplus: Stapleford's ~£5/yr operating surplus is held in trust and banks to Abisec's reserve meanwhile.
provisioning.accounts: Bascar (Abisec's retired father, resident lord of Stapleford) keeps the Stapleford books — a real managed pipeline.

key_npcs.name: Mabli
key_npcs.note: see characters.json -- childhood friend, ledgers-genius; runs Hindon's books

key_npcs.name: Sir Bledig
key_npcs.note: see characters.json -- Idnerth's old seneschal, retained; honest, knows every parcel & penny

key_npcs.name: Drustan
key_npcs.personality: Grizzled veteran spearman, blunt and unsmiling; drills the garrison hard and feeds his men first; cares nothing for court, everything for a tight watch. Loyal to a lord who respects the men on the wall.

key_npcs.name: Gwgan the Wool-master
key_npcs.personality: Shrewd, prosperous, calculating -- but honest since Abisec purged the wool-fraud and cut the mill-toll. The staple's voice; wants stability above all (stability is profit). A useful barometer of the town's mood.

key_npcs.name: Rhiwallon
key_npcs.personality: Meticulous, dry, incorruptible -- installed to keep the staple's weights & tolls honest after the factor's fraud. Trusts a ledger over a face.

key_npcs.name: Heilyn the Miller
key_npcs.personality: Competent, prosperous, faintly resented (millers take toll); watched since the mill-toll was cut and the hand-querns outlawed. Keeps his head down and the wheel turning.

key_npcs.name: Einion the Reeve
key_npcs.personality: Solid, honest peasant foreman; knows every furrow, tenant, and feud in the vill. The lord's eyes on the land; speaks plainly when asked and not otherwise.

key_npcs.name: Tudur the Smith
key_npcs.personality: Strong, taciturn, indispensable -- arms, tools, horseshoes. Says little, makes much.

key_npcs.name: Gwrgi
key_npcs.personality: Dour, weather-bitten shepherd-reeve of the high downs; suspicious of town men and new lords alike, but fair with his own.

storm_damage_483.dead: ~4 townsfolk (Tegwen's family) drowned in the lower wool-town
storm_damage_483.wall_breach: town-side moat-bank washed out -> breach in the new wool-town wall. PATCHED early winter 483 with a timber-and-rubble palisade (rough but a wall again; DV ~3-4 at that section until the spring stone rebuild restores DV 5).
storm_damage_483.losses: 3 houses; the staple's lower wool-store ruined; ~12 of the new vaccary cattle drowned in the flooded enclosure
storm_damage_483.repair_detail: Mabli CRIT costing: urgent breach PATCH ~£1 (done, early winter 483; storm's own stone+timber + free town labor) + spring proper work ~£5 (stone wall rebuild ~£3, mill ~£1, cattle restock ~£2). Wool-store: not all lost — Mabli salvages & sells the wet wool cheap (~£3 income dent, not a repair).
storm_damage_483.status_resolved: REPAIRED by spring 483 — wall rebuilt (DV5), mill mended, ~12 cattle restocked off Cadwal; the dead mourned. Total cost ~£6.

key_npcs.note: see characters.json -- runs Stapleford for Abisec

key_npcs.name: Eluned
key_npcs.note: see characters.json -- keeper of the old rite, healer

key_npcs.name: Maredudd the Reeve
key_npcs.personality: Long-serving, steady, unhurried; Bascar's right hand and the vill's memory. Has run Stapleford's fields through three harvests of trouble without complaint.

key_npcs.name: Iorwerth
key_npcs.personality: A reformed poacher turned keeper -- knows every run and snare because he set them once. Sly, loyal, good with ferrets and excuses.

key_npcs.name: Gwilym Hafod
key_npcs.personality: Quiet, patient, proud of the birds beyond all reason; speaks more gently to a hawk than to a man. Keeper of the hawk-and-icicles line.

key_npcs.name: Selyf the Armorer
key_npcs.personality: Methodical, exacting, a little vain about his work; the armory is his kingdom and his blades are honest.
